card.name: Interval numbers before "-minute intervals"
card.fires_on: A spelled-out or digit number (two, six, three, 6) right after "at" or "approximately" that gives the spacing between repeated doses, just before a word like minute, hour, or month intervals. Also the hyphen or second number in a range such as "two- to three-minute".

modes.label: Number after "at"
modes.description: A number word that starts a repeat-dose interval phrase.
modes.example: Additional doses of 1.25 mg may be administered at<< six>> hour intervals.

modes.label: Hyphen or range part
modes.description: The hyphen or second number within a range of interval lengths.
modes.example: may be repeated at two-to<<-three>>-minute intervals.

card.writes: It promotes hyphen-joined compound endings like -person, -digit and -point, so it favors a hyphenated unit word after the number.
card.plain: It fires on the number that says how many minutes or hours apart repeat doses are given.
